cluster_summary: Judged from code, the open ground in this cluster is narrow and operational rather than methodological: ship2shore_rag's free, legally-sourced, offline-shippable maritime corpus (MAIB/NTSB/NtM ingestion + SQLite vessel snapshot) and repo-traffic-analytics' CI-checkout and owner-activity subtraction are the two pieces with no packaged equivalent found. ship2shore_rag does now implement dense+sparse RRF hybrid retrieval with cross-encoder rerank and an eval harness, but the method itself was published for maritime accident reports in June 2026 (arXiv:2606.13249), and only its vessel path uses true BM25 (the shore path uses Postgres ts_rank). claude-lmstudio-router is now fully superseded: LM Studio 0.4.1 (its own target) and Ollama both serve native Anthropic /v1/messages for Claude Code. memory-map-optimizer's search re-implements what qmd already ships (BM25+vector, RRF k=60, Qwen3 reranker). The biggest README-vs-code gaps are in data_validator (Kaggle 'discovery' is a hardcoded list, cross-source consistency samples 20 symbols x 5 dates with exceptions swallowed, leakage detection is line regexes), cache_memory_cleaner (archive-evict 'byte-verifies' by size only before rm -rf), claude-provenance ('tamper-evidence' hashes are recomputed on re-ingest), and blog-consistency-check (screenshot baselines are never diffed). Roughly 13 of the 33 repos are infra, docs, data stubs or personal files with no survey question; cloud-map is public but maps personal cloud folders and should be private.

repos.does: Ingests arXiv, Wikipedia, UK MAIB, NTSB (via CAROL's JSON endpoint), UKHO Notices to Mariners and local files; chunks to 220-word windows, embeds with all-MiniLM-L6-v2, and retrieves by fusing pgvector cosine with Postgres full-text (shore) or sqlite-vec with FTS5 BM25 (vessel snapshot) via RRF, then cross-encoder rerank, then a per-source/near-duplicate diversity cut; optional Claude answer with a no-LLM [n] citation checker. Also carries a separate vessel operations CRUD module and a Kafka->DuckDB telemetry sketch.

claims_vs_code.claim: Hybrid BM25+dense retrieval (the August brief's recommendation)
claims_vs_code.evidence: Implemented, but only the vessel/SQLite path is true BM25 (FTS5 'ORDER BY rank', retrieval/sqlite_store.py:159). The default shore path ranks the sparse side with Postgres ts_rank (retrieval/retriever.py:43-51), a term-frequency score, not BM25.

claims_vs_code.claim: Retrieval quality is measurable (Recall@k/MRR, MRR 0.633->0.933 with rerank, CHANGELOG.md:657)
claims_vs_code.evidence: Harness is real (eval/evaluate.py) but eval/queries.yaml holds 17 hand-picked queries with exactly one expected URL each; numbers are from a tiny single-annotator set, not a benchmark.
Applied as a post-filter after RRF (retrieval/retriever.py:97-111, docstring admits it can shrink the pool below top_k); not pushed down into the SQL.

repos.maturity_note: 23 test files run in CI (quality-gates.yml lists them explicitly), 53 commits, real eval harness and committed SQLite snapshot; last code commit Oct 2026.

snippets.why: The shore-side hybrid core: Postgres full-text rank and pgvector cosine rank fused with 1/(k+rank) Reciprocal Rank Fusion (Cormack et al. 2009), the same fusion used by the 2606.13249 maritime RAG paper; note rank is 0-based and the sparse side is ts_rank, not BM25.
Final top-k cut after cross-encoder rerank: per-source cap plus SequenceMatcher near-duplicate skip, a greedy diversity filter in the spirit of MMR but text-overlap based rather than embedding based.

    fi
